subject: Y1
name: Trumbull — sunlit stone, precise architectural watercolor

styleSelection.reason: The central gable, paired Gothic arches and chimney junctions need dry, fitted edges. Transparent warm wall planes and connected cool shadow glazes carry the building; selective fine sepia carries sub-brush mullions.

families.referenceCue: Pale cerulean sky with irregular cloud lights between the roofs. One flowing graded wash on a measured dry base, watery transparent pigment and merging own-stroke overlap; reserve cloud lights and protect sharp roof silhouettes. Do not require an initially moist whole footprint, because the sky color family also contains cool roof and glass shapes.

Connected ochre and raw-sienna masonry planes across the building. Broad transparent washes, then dry mid planes and cross-boundary blue-brown shadow glazes; ashlar is a few pale irregular hints, not a grid.
Sunlit central gable and paired pointed arches are the focus. Keep the front pale and warm, the narrow slits and arches cool and dark on dry paper; pale rims and window divisions survive.
Tall left chimney, slate roof and receding wall form the major connected shadow side. Dry glazes cross stone, eaves, window surrounds and the lower wall; retain the narrow lit chimney face.
Right chimney and repeated windows are secondary architecture. Paint fitted wall and roof planes, then dry recesses; window frames are fine lines rather than thick painted bands.
Low annex has a pale slate roof, bright upper cornice and warm front against dark rectangular windows. Preserve its light roof edge; shadow glazes connect eave and openings.

Yellow-green tree overlaps the central wall and annex. Keep the fitted irregular canopy and sky/wall gaps; connected olive shadow groups after drying, with only a few crisp leaf edges. No pen filling the canopy.
Thin light pavement strip and tiny figures anchor the building. Pale connected ground, a restrained dry grounding glaze, and only target-sized dark accents; do not invent grass texture.

reserves.reason: Small near-paper glint on the annex slate roof, following its real bright edge
Small cream highlight on the central left arch rim; the rest of the rim stays a pale painted plane
